subject: Vendor gap snapshot + smoking-gun tests
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Porter <jenna.porter@averyhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor gap snapshot + smoking-gun tests

Hi Jenna —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Writing up a short recap so we’re all aligned on priorities, known gaps, and the concrete tests we propose running in the bakeoff window.

TL;DR (ask): please confirm the three smoking-gun tests below and share the de-identified prompt set if you’re comfortable; we’ll schedule infra and send a draft runbook by Tuesday.

Key pain points you reiterated
- Unreliable long-context continuity in triage flows (loss of prior patient context beyond ~6–7k tokens).
- P95 latency spikes during burst triage loads — must keep p95 under ~150ms for live triage.
- Cost sensitivity at scale; target unit economics need to be < $X per 1M tokens to justify full rollout.
- Compliance needs: 1yr audit log retention, VPC/private deployment option, and SOC2 artifacts for procurement.

Primary goals for decision committee
1) Match or beat current latency & availability (p95 <150ms, SLO 99.5% uptime).
2) Maintain answer quality parity (clinical hallucination rate <= baseline).
3) Predictable unit cost at production scale.
4) Private/VPC deployment and auditability.

Decision criteria (what they’ll score on)
- Latency (p95), throughput at scale, and consistency
- Output quality on a curated clinical prompt set (hallucination / factuality probes)
- Cost per token at 95th percentile throughput
- Deployment model & security posture (VPC, KMS, audit logs)

Competitive observations from conversation
- BeaconAI: very fast in short contexts; their billed cost is higher; caching seems aggressive but behavior diverges on long-context continuity.
- Nimbus Labs: strong throughput optimizations but we heard memory pressure leads to degraded outputs in long-context tests.
- OrbitAI: balanced but misses on private-deploy flexibility and audit log granularity.

Suggested smoking-gun tests (proposed owners in parens)
1) Long-context continuity: 20k token clinical-dialog chain test across 500 cases — measure % context retention, hallucination regression, and token growth behavior. (Eng: Karthik / SE: Marissa)
2) Sustained burst throughput: 200 concurrent sessions for 30 minutes at production prompt mix — report p50/p95/p99 latency and error/retry rates. (Eng: Karthik)
3) Quality A/B: 500 de-identified clinical vignettes run against vendor baseline (BeaconAI) and Redwood quantized stack — measure hallucination rate, top-1 factual accuracy, and parsimony. (SE: Marissa)

Files I’m attaching: bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx (scoring rubric), redwood-performance-snapshot.pdf (prelim perf numbers), and a short draft runbook template.

Open questions for your team (Jenna)
- Can you confirm the test region preference (we assume us-east)?
- Can you share a de-identified prompt set or accept our minimal de-id template?
- Any procurement hard deadlines we should know about?

Proposed next steps
- We’ll lock test owners and reserved infra slots once you confirm the prompt set and region (target by Tue 7/14).
- Internal kick-off to run the long-context test: Thu 7/16 — we’ll invite engineering.
- Follow-up readout with your decision committee scheduled week of 7/27 (tentative).

Thanks — happy to hop on a 15-min follow-up if that helps.

—
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: bakeoff-scorecard.xlsx (stated), redwood-performance-snapshot.pdf (stated)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Vendor gap snapshot + smoking-gun tests

Thanks Soojin — great summary. A few clarifications and owners below.

I’ll own the quality A/B (test #3) and put together a randomized evaluation harness for hallucination / factuality metrics. I’ll also produce the side-by-side scorecard we’ll use for the committee.

Karthik — can you provision a dedicated test slot for Thu 7/16 (2-hour window) and a larger sustained run on Mon 7/20 (30-minute sustained burst)? We’ll need GPU reservation and a reproducible script to drive the 200 concurrent sessions.

Notes on what we’ll run for vendor comparisons (internal)
- Redwood config: redwood-q8-optimized + kv-cache enabled (seeded with patient context).
- Beacon baseline: beacon-opt-16 (their latest pub note).
- Nimbus: if they can provide a test endpoint we’ll include them otherwise mark as qualitative only.

Action items (owners)
- Marissa: A/B harness + scorecard (deliver by 7/15).
- Karthik: infra reservations + runbook hooks (deliver by 7/14).
- Soojin: coordinate prompt set and confirm region with Avery (in flight).

One more ask: Jenna, if procurement needs SOC2/Security artifacts before we start tests, point me to the right person so I can get those to you ASAP.

—
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Vendor gap snapshot + smoking-gun tests

Soojin / Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. We’re aligned on the priorities you listed. A few quick points from our side:

1) Region: yes, please run tests in us-east (primary). We want latency numbers from the same cloud region our prod endpoints will be in.
2) Prompt set: I attached a de-identified sample (avery-deid-prompts.csv) — it’s a 250-row extract, enough for a dry run. We’ll work on sharing the full 500-case set after a short mutual NDA addendum (procurement will send).
3) Procurement timeline: decision committee meets 2026-08-01; procurement is trying to close commercial terms the week after.

We accept the three smoking-gun tests as the decision-critical items. For the long-context continuity test — please include a side-by-side token-trace export so we can inspect how the vendor manages KV growth.

Also flagging a security ask: procurement will want to see KMS integration details and an export of audit log samples for the last 30 days. If you can pre-stage SOC2 evidence that will accelerate the procurement window.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the runbook and the proposed test schedule.

—
Jenna Porter
Director, Clinical Integrations
Avery Health
jenna.porter@averyhealth.com

Attachments: avery-deid-prompts.csv (de-identified sample)

- Thu 7/16 10:00-12:00 PDT — Long-context continuity dry run (20k token, 250 cases).
- Mon 7/20 09:00-09:30 PDT — Sustained burst (200 concurrent sessions, 30 min).

Deliverables we’ll produce and share after each run:
